question.problem: The owner of a restaurant noted that $145$ vegetarian customers visited his restaurant during a particular week. On a particular day of the same week, he noted that $x=15$ vegetarian customers visited the restaurant, corresponding to a $z$-score of $z=-1.5.$ Find the standard deviation of the number of vegetarian customers per day, giving your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the mean number of vegetarian customers for each day:

$$
\overset{¯}{x}=\frac{145}{7}=20.71
$$

to $2$ decimal places.

The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z=\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma }.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set. Rewriting this in terms of $\sigma ,$ we get

$$
\sigma =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{z}.
$$

So, the standard deviation $\sigma $ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\frac{x-\overset{¯}{x}}{z} \\  & =\frac{15-20.71}{-1.5} \\  & =3.81\end{aligned}
$$

 
to $2$ decimal places.
